open_points.subject: public_op:effects.operation_element_conclusion
open_points.text: "Outputs: Its conclusion: succeeded with outputs; failed with its status ... waiting with its reason; or not reached"
open_points.question: When the element is waiting for owner approval, must this operation also return the waiting approval_id (so runs can build run answers without reading effect-owned records directly)?
options: Return waiting reason plus approval_id for owner_approval
open_points.default_guess: Return waiting reason plus approval_id for owner_approval.

open_points.subject: MCP operation read_spooled_file
open_points.text: "the lookup identity; its digest, size and media type only describe it"
open_points.question: If the caller supplies digest/size/media_type that do not match the located SpooledFile record, should the call refuse or ignore those descriptive fields?
options: Ignore descriptive fields; use lookup identity only
Refuse when any descriptive field mismatches
open_points.default_guess: Ignore descriptive fields and use only the lookup identity.

open_points.subject: MCP operation get_flow
open_points.text: "get_flow ... calls flows.active_flow_version, flows.read_flow_version: the flow's purpose, its active version and FlowActivation, or that none is active"
open_points.question: For an active flow, does get_flow return the full active FlowVersion graph or only activation metadata/ids?
options: Return full active FlowVersion (ports/nodes/edges/constants) plus activation
Return only flow metadata + active flow_version_id + activation
open_points.default_guess: Return full active FlowVersion plus activation, since flows.read_flow_version is explicitly called.

open_points.subject: State 5 Conventions (refusal vs internal_error)
open_points.text: "A refusal is decided before the operation's first store change, so it writes nothing" and "When a request makes several store changes, those made before the failed one stay"
open_points.question: Is internal_error outside the 'refusal writes nothing' rule, or must operations guarantee no prior writes when returning internal_error?
options: internal_error is exempt; earlier committed changes may remain
internal_error must also imply no writes at all
open_points.default_guess: internal_error is exempt; earlier successful store changes remain.

open_points.subject: MCP get_repair_view pagination
open_points.text: "... with a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page; passed back, it pages only the NodeExecutions below that position for that set ..."
open_points.question: If the caller changes page size between continuation calls for get_repair_view, is that allowed (as in list_records) or refused for this operation?
options: Refuse continuation when page size differs from the first page
